messages.subject: Folder organisation - subfolders
parts:
Hi all, I was wondering if anyone would be so kind as to help me something I'm stuck on with camTrapR. I'm quite new to R so bear with me if any queries seem basic.

I'm trying to create a record table initially, based on how I have arranged my "directory". This was images saved in to a main folder and two sub folders as: camera station - species - number of individuals. I think creating a record table hasn't worked how I want due to the additional subfolder of number of individuals of that species,  seen at each station. 

I want this info to show in the record table (for each camera station - the different species and when they occur alone, in pairs, in threes etc). This is important to represent. Is there a way to do this? It seems it can only be categorised as far as different species

Many thanks in advance
H

Hi Helen!
I have no experience with folder-subfolder arrangement, but I use metadata tags and I have no problem adding group information. I create a different tag for group information, with numbers as levels. Making a paralelism with subfolders approach I guess the problem you've found is in the multiple hierarchy inside "species". Maybe you could try creating a full new group of subfolders inside a "group" information folder. Hope this helps!

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Folder organisation - subfolders
parts:
Hi Helen & Lucia,
when you use the species folder approach for identifying species, you cannot have subfolders within the species folders. This is because camtrapR will use the folder name as the species name. So I suppose the entries in the species column are "1", "2", etc.?

Lucia is right, it would be easier to add group size and other information with the metadata tagging approach. Even though you identified images by folder already, you can still add other metadata tags for additional information (like group size) to the images, it will be reported in the record table. 

Here is a possible way forward in your situation:

1. assign the group size to all images as metadata. I'm afraid you'll have to do this manually in digiKam, but you can assign the group size to all images in a group size subfolder at once. It may be possible to write some exiftool code to do this, but I don't have any code ready to achieve this)
2. move all images from the group size subfolders to the species folders. That can be automated in R. Below is some code for that purpose (please test if first or make a backup before applying the code):

Let us know how it goes please
Cheers,
Jürgen

library(stringi)

# define image directory
wd_images_ID <- "..."   # define image directory

# find all image filenames
filenames_full <- list.files(wd_images_ID, full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, pattern = ".JPG$")
filenames_short <- basename(filenames_full)

# find their directories
directory_of_files <- dirname(filenames)

# make data.frame
df_tmp <- data.frame(filename_full = filenames_full,
                     directory = directory_of_files,
                     filename_short = filenames_short,
                     directory_to = NA,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# find last character of directory name
last_character <- stri_sub(df_tmp$directory, from = -1, to = -1)   

# which images are in a group size directory (drectory name end with a number)?   # gives a warning but that's ok
which_last_character_number <- which(!is.na(as.numeric(last_character)))

# define output directory: if image is in a group size directory, find its parent diretory (species directory), Otherwise change nothing
df_tmp$directory_to[which_last_character_number]  <- dirname(df_tmp$directory[which_last_character_number])
df_tmp$directory_to[-which_last_character_number] <- df_tmp$directory[-which_last_character_number]


# move files from group size to species directory (does not rename in this case, only moves files)
file.rename(from = df_tmp$filename_full[which_last_character_number],
            to = file.path(df_tmp$directory_to, df_tmp$filename_short)[which_last_character_number])
